label: Yemen War Total Deaths (est., cumulative since 2015)
source: UN Development Programme / UN News, Dec 2021
contestNote: ~60% attributed to indirect causes (famine, disease, lack of healthcare); Saudi-led coalition disputes indirect-cause methodology. ACLED's narrower direct-violence tally separately recorded 70,000+ direct fatalities. Figure pre-dates the 2026 escalation.

label: Govt. Troops Killed, Marib/Hadramout (Aug 6)
source: Yemeni government / AFP military source / Houthi claim
contestNote: Government confirmed 30 killed, 50 wounded; unnamed military source told AFP toll may reach 58; Houthis claim 45 killed. Deadliest single episode of the conflict in years.

label: Killed in Bab al-Mandeb 'Double-Tap' Strike (Aug 11)
source: Yemen government / Al Jazeera / NBC News
deltaNote: 4 crew (3 Pakistani, 1 Indonesian) + 2 Yemeni coast guard rescuers killed on the cargo ship Tihamah. First fatal Houthi attack on shipping since the Iran war began Feb 28.

label: Civilians Wounded, Najran (Aug 7)
source: Saudi Press Agency / Saudi-led Coalition Joint Forces Command
deltaNote: 7 Saudis (incl. a 4-year-old with 2nd-degree burns), 1 Yemeni, 2 Egyptians, 1 Pakistani. Highest civilian toll inside Saudi Arabia in over four years.

label: People in Need of Humanitarian Assistance
source: UN OCHA — Yemen Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026
deltaNote: Includes 5.2M internally displaced persons, 329,000 migrants, and 63,000 refugees/asylum seekers. 2026 appeal is barely 20% funded.

label: Brent Crude Price
deltaNote: Peaked near $100/bbl on Jul 23 after the Saudi tanker strikes, eased to ~$89 by mid-August, then ticked back up after the Aug 24 Houthi missile strike on the VLCC Amzan off Yanbu — though the market reaction was muted versus July, as traders distinguished the contained vessel fire from a wider export shutdown.

label: Red Sea Maritime Defence Coalition Signatories
deltaNote: 43 of 51 invited states plus the EU attended the Jul 30 Riyadh summit; 14 signed the founding statement incl. Turkiye, Egypt, Pakistan, Jordan, Bangladesh. UAE and Oman did not join.

label: Civilians Killed/Wounded, US Strikes (2025 campaign)
source: Pentagon review via Washington Post, Aug 11, 2026
contestNote: First Trump administration public acknowledgment of significant civilian harm from US operations. Pentagon found 3 April 2025 strikes 'more likely than not' caused civilian harm but denied condolence payments; 15 further incidents remain under investigation.

Yemenis Facing Food Insecurity

label: Government Operations vs. Houthis (24h, Aug 20)
source: Yemeni military spokesman Gen. Majid Abdullah al-Nuzaili / Al Jazeera
contestNote: Government-reported operation and casualty ('neutralized' fighters/commanders) tally; not independently verified. Followed a claimed 181 operations on Aug 16.
